subject: Archaeology
title: LiDAR: Lasers Through the Jungle
description: A 60-second lesson on LiDAR: Lasers Through the Jungle.

hook.text: A laser fired from an airplane can strip away virtual jungle and reveal ancient cities hidden under the canopy.

buildup.text: LiDAR fires millions of laser pulses per second. Some pass through gaps in tree cover and bounce off the ground below.

discovery.text: In 2018, LiDAR revealed 60,000 previously unknown Maya structures under Guatemalan jungle, including pyramids and roads.

twist.text: The scans showed the Maya lowlands held millions of people — up to 10 times more than previously estimated.

climax.text: LiDAR is now revealing hidden cities across Southeast Asia, Central America, and Africa in a matter of hours.

punchline.text: Lasers from the sky see through forests. Entire civilizations were hiding under the trees.

quiz.question: What did LiDAR reveal under Guatemala's jungle in 2018?
options: A single massive Maya pyramid larger than any previously known
60,000 previously unknown Maya structures including pyramids and roads
A network of underground tunnels connecting Maya cities

details.summary: LiDAR fires millions of laser pulses from aircraft through vegetation to map ground surfaces with centimeter accuracy. In archaeology, it has revealed hidden cities, road networks, and agricultural systems beneath tropical forests in Central America, Southeast Asia, and elsewhere.
details.whyItMatters: LiDAR has been called the most transformative technology in archaeology since radiocarbon dating. It reveals entire landscapes of human activity hidden under forest canopy, fundamentally changing our understanding of past civilizations.
takeaways: Laser pulses penetrate vegetation to map ground surfaces precisely
Revealed hidden Maya and Khmer cities beneath jungle canopy
Considered the most transformative archaeological technology in decades

faq.question: How does LiDAR see through dense forest?
faq.answer: Millions of laser pulses are fired from an aircraft. Most reflect off leaves and branches, but some penetrate gaps and reach the ground. Software filters out vegetation returns, leaving only ground-level reflections. The result is a bare-earth terrain model showing features hidden by trees.

faq.question: What major discoveries has LiDAR made possible?
faq.answer: LiDAR revealed that Angkor in Cambodia was surrounded by a city of over 1,000 square kilometers. In Guatemala, it tripled estimates of Maya population. In the Amazon, it showed pre-Columbian earthworks across supposedly pristine forest. Each survey rewrites regional archaeology.
